stipulates the information that must be written on all credit agreements

use brown flour instead of white flour

questionText: Indicate with a tick (✓) whether each of the following statements is true or false.
stem: Supplementary welfare allowance is means tested. Child benefit is a universal welfare payment. Working family payment is available to employees on low pay with children.

rows.verbatim: Supplementary welfare allowance is means tested — True
rows.contextNote: Graded 2:0, so a tick is worth 2 or nothing — there is no half mark on this question. Supplementary Welfare Allowance is paid only after your means have been assessed, so the tick goes in the True column.

rows.verbatim: Child benefit is a universal welfare payment — True
rows.contextNote: True. Universal means paid for every child whatever the family earns, and Child Benefit is not means tested — which is the contrast this question is testing against the payment above.

rows.verbatim: Working family payment is available to employees on low pay with children — True
rows.contextNote: True. Working Family Payment tops up the wages of an employee on low pay who has children. All three statements here are true, so a candidate who split the ticks between the columns looking for a pattern gave marks away.

notes: Each statement carries its own 2 marks, so fixed: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. The scheme ticks all three True; the statement is quoted verbatim and the ticked column stated after an em dash, which is how a tick/circle answer is carried elsewhere in the deck. Graded 2:0 means all-or-nothing per statement, noted on r-1. The statements are in the stem because the question cannot be attempted without them, and they leak no answer — the answer is which column is ticked.

goods not owned until final payment is made

questionText: Discuss three advantages of a positive parent-child relationship within the family.

rows.verbatim: Discuss three advantages of a positive parent-child relationship within the family
rows.contextNote: Three advantages at 5 marks. Every point on this list runs the same way — something the child gains now that carries into later life — and the 5 is in that second half. Secure attachment now, healthy relationships later; emotional regulation now, coping under stress later. An advantage stated without its consequence is a 3.

options: children feel valued as they can express their feelings in a safe environment
secure and healthy attachment to their parents
develop happy and content relationships with others in life
child learns to regulate emotions under stress and in difficult situations
establish secure bonds and friendships with peers
promote a child’s cognitive, emotional, and social development

notes: One flat list, evenly priced.
